Stretch Tracker is a fitness plus ergonomics app without any monthly subscription and hidden fees.  It is different from any of the fitness app that you have tried in the past.  It  uses your camera video and computer vision to estimate pose, action, muscle stretch, joint strain and calorie values.  Try for yourself and find out how the app evaluates your muscle stretch and joint strain real time without the need for uploading video file or secondary processing. 
INSTRUCTION
1.	Mount you iPhone/iPad in a stand in the floor so it can see your entire body.  
2.	Go to the setting page by clicking on the ring of circles.  
3.	Enter your body weight, height and exercise time in the settings page.  
4.	Use the front camera to evaluate your muscle stretch and joint strain during exercise.  
5.	Use the back camera to take exercise data from a recorded video or image played in your TV or PC or real time exercise data for others.  
6.	Leave the angle threshold values unchanged.  
7.	Hit the play button and move your arms to get the pose estimation model predict body joints.
BODY POSE ESTIMATION
Stretch Tracker uses iOS 14 pose estimation model to estimate 19 joint position real time - left wrist, left elbow, left shoulder, neck, right shoulder, right elbow, right wrist, left hip, root, right hip, left knee, left ankle, right knee, right ankle, left ear, left eye, right eye, right ear and nose.
REAL TIME JOINT STRAIN & MUSCLE STRETCH 
The relative distance, angles between the joints and their positions is used to calculate dynamics of motion such as displacement, speed and calorie burned.  Muscle stretch is displayed by different color from blue to red - indicating low stretch to high stretch in units of ft or cm.  Joint strain is displayed by different color from blue to red indicating joint angle relative to threshold angle between the joints.  The threshold angle values for shoulder, elbow, back and knee can be adjusted in the settings page. The joint color and muscle color (line joining the joints) represent different things so they may not align .  While joint color to red indicates bending a joint above its threshold level, the muscle line color represents degree of movement of the joints, which is a measure of amount of exercise and calorie burned.
ACTION RECOGNITION
Based on different joint positions and your exercise type seven different actions are recognized: standing, sitting, hand stretching, squat, lunges and bending.  Note that action is recognized real time based on current position between the joints, so if the position changes, the action shows a different value.
STRAIN & STRETCH ANALYSIS PIE CHART VIEW
Two pie charts one for joint strain and the other for muscle stretch are displayed real time.  Muscle stretch pie chart shows hand, legs and abs muscles movement (in ft or cm) in green, yellow and red color segments.  Joint strain pie chart shows shoulder, elbow, back and knee joint strain time in seconds in orange, teal, purple and pink color segments.
CALORIE ESTIMATION & TIME
Calorie is estimated by calculating relative displacement of each muscle segment and their relative weight.  Calorie estimation is instantaneous and is displayed in the menu bar in between the two pie charts.  The time settings can be changed from the settings page and time is entered in seconds.  The time remaining is shown when the play button is pressed.
TRACK YOUR FITESS
The fitness summary is saved in a table format that you can use to track exercises in different time. The table shows the date, time, exercise type, calories, abs flex (abdomen stretch)  in appropriate units (ft or cm) and the most strained joint during the exercise.  The exercise type and joint strain values stored in the table are the most frequent exercise type and joint strain during the time period and these values can be different than current values.

All data and definitions are based on the Updated Breast Chapter - AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition, released on November 10th, 2017 that included the classic Anatomic Stage Group and the new and revolutionary Prognostic Stage Group (divided in Clinical Prognostic Stage and Pathological Prognostic Stage) with the incorporation of biomarker factors that predict more accurately cancer outcome for a more personalized and precise approach. 
 
The prognostic factors included in the new TNM are: Tumor Grade (G), HER2, Estrogen Receptor (ER) and Progesterone Receptor (PR). Genomic Profiles were also incorporated as a prognostic factor for eligible cases (pT1-T2 N0 M0 HER2- and ER+) in the Pathological Prognostic Stage.

The Anatomic Stage is based solely on the anatomic extent of cancer as defined by the T, N, and M categories and should be used for all patients even if prognostic staging is possible.
 
The Clinical Prognostic Stage will be used to assign stage for all patients based on history, physical examination, imaging studies, and relevant biopsies. Clinical Prognostic Stage is determined by cT, cN, c/pM, G, HER2, ER, and PR. Genomic profile information is not included in Clinical Prognostic Stage.
 
The Pathological Prognostic Stage will be used to assign stage for patients who have the surgical resection as the initial treatment of their cancer before any systemic or radiation therapy. It includes all information used for clinical staging plus findings at surgery and pathological findings from surgical resection. Pathological Prognostic Stage is determined by pT, pN, c/pM, G, HER2, ER, and PR. Genomic profile information can be used for the Pathological Prognostic Stage (pT1-T2 N0, HER2- and ER+). Pathological Prognostic Stage does not apply to patients treated with chemotherapy, hormone therapy or radiation prior to surgical resection (neoadjuvant therapy).
 
This App provides the quantification of the category change of the Clinical Prognosis Stage (cPS) and also the Pathological Prognostic Stage (pPS) in relation to the Anatomic Stage (AS) expressed in the Staging Line with the symbol +1, +2, +3 in case of worsening in the Prognostic Staging or -1, -2, -3 in case of improvement in the Prognostic Staging.
